_comment: What every migration this fork added did, and what has to happen for official Sonarr to run on
a database that has seen it. tools/rollback-to-official.py reads this and acts only on the
migrations a given database actually recorded in VersionInfo.
Adding a migration means adding it here. ForkMigrationRollbackPlanFixture fails the build
otherwise, so this cannot quietly fall behind.
adds        what the migration created, for the record
inert       true when official Sonarr can run with it left in place, which is the case for
every plain column: they are NOT NULL with a default, and Sonarr names the
columns it knows when it inserts
blocks      a query that must return no rows before rollback, with the reason and what to do
undo        statements to run, in order, once nothing blocks

9001.name: add_series_edition

blocks.query: SELECT Id, Title, EditionName, Path FROM Series WHERE EditionName <> ''
blocks.label: editions
blocks.reason: This migration dropped IX_Series_TvdbId, which official Sonarr relies on: it looks a series up with SingleOrDefault, and that throws the moment two rows share a TVDB id - during a metadata refresh, a release parse, an import.
blocks.resolution: Delete each of these from Sonarr itself. A series has rows in a dozen tables and only Sonarr removes it properly; deleting the series does not have to delete its files.

undo: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "IX_Series_TvdbId" ON "Series" ("TvdbId" ASC)

9010.name: add_episode_file_parts
9010.note: 9011 renamed PartNumber to MultipleNumber and dropped VersionName, so only the table is left to deal with.

9011.name: episode_file_multiples

warns.query: SELECT Id, SeriesId, RelativePath FROM EpisodeFiles WHERE MultipleType <> 0 AND Id NOT IN (SELECT EpisodeFileId FROM Episodes)
warns.label: extra part files
warns.reason: Official Sonarr deletes any file row no episode points at, then finds the file still on disk and imports it again on top of the part that was already there.
warns.resolution: The rows go below. The files stay on disk - move them elsewhere first if they should not come back as ordinary files.

undo: DELETE FROM EpisodeFiles WHERE MultipleType <> 0 AND Id NOT IN (SELECT EpisodeFileId FROM Episodes)
